alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism despite levothyroxine
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5) with low free T4, tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes — consistent with inadequately treated hypothyroidism. She reports often forgetting her levothyroxine. The plan to simply continue levothyroxine 50 mcg without addressing adherence or dose escalation will not correct this. Much of the weight gain (9 kg/year), low mood, and metabolic disturbance may be driven by hypothyroidism rather than DTG. Non-adherence to levothyroxine is the most likely cause of the current presentation.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel on levothyroxine adherence, increase dose (e.g., to 75 mcg), and recheck TSH/free T4 in 6–8 weeks before attributing weight gain to DTG.

alerts.title: DTG switch for weight gain may be premature
alerts.message: The clinician plans to switch from DTG due to weight gain. However, the patient's symptoms (tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, delayed reflexes) and elevated TSH strongly suggest hypothyroidism as the primary driver of weight gain and metabolic changes. Switching from DTG prematurely risks compromising a virologically suppressive regimen (viral load <50) without addressing the underlying thyroid dysfunction. Guidelines list abnormal weight gain as a DTG side effect, but attribution here is confounded by uncontrolled hypothyroidism and poor levothyroxine adherence.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise hypothyroidism management first; reassess weight and symptoms before considering a DTG switch. Viral load is suppressed — avoid unnecessary regimen change.

alerts.title: Amitriptyline may worsen constipation and weight gain
alerts.message: Patient takes amitriptyline 50 mg and reports constipation. Amitriptyline has anticholinergic properties that commonly cause or worsen constipation. Concurrent uncontrolled hypothyroidism also causes constipation, creating a compounding risk for bowel dysfunction. Additionally, amitriptyline is associated with weight gain, which may further confound attribution of weight gain to DTG. The combination of hypothyroidism, amitriptyline, and possible DTG-related weight gain creates multiple overlapping contributors to the patient's presentation.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess whether amitriptyline contributes to constipation and weight gain; consider alternative antidepressants with lower metabolic burden if clinically appropriate.

alerts.title: Elevated lipids with obesity warrant monitoring plan
alerts.message: Patient has elevated LDL cholesterol 4.2 mmol/L and total cholesterol 6.4 mmol/L, with BMI 33. TDF-based regimens are less dyslipidaemic than alternatives, but if DTG is switched to an EFV-based or protease inhibitor-based regimen, lipid profiles may worsen. Current lipid elevations in the context of obesity and hypothyroidism warrant baseline documentation and monitoring. No lipid follow-up plan is documented. Hypothyroidism itself can elevate lipids, and correcting TSH may improve the lipid profile.

evidence.recommended_action: Document baseline lipids, optimise thyroid function, and plan repeat lipid panel after thyroid correction before any ART switch.
